&options) {\n  CHECK_COLLECTION_READONLY_RETURN_STATUS;\n\n  std::lock_guard lock(schema_handle_mtx_);\n  // when optimizing, schema operations(include another optimize) are not\n  // allowed\n\n  CHECK_DESTROY_RETURN_STATUS(destroyed_, false);\n\n  std::vector<Segment::Ptr> persist_segments;\n\n  {\n    // forbidden writing for a while\n    std::lock_guard write_lock(write_mtx_);\n\n    if FileHelper::MakeTempSegmentPath(path_, tmp_segment_id);\n\n          auto new_segment_id = allocate_segment_id();\n          auto new_segment_path =\n              FileHelper::MakeSegmentPath(path_,        create_index_task.output_segment_meta_);\n        CHECK_RETURN_STATUS(s);\n      }\n    }\n\n    // 2. update version\n    s = version_manager_->apply(new_version);\n segment_manager_->destroy_segment(input_segment->id());\n          CHECK_RETURN_STATUS(s);\n        }\n      } else if (std::holds_alternative<CreateVectorIndexTask>(task_info)) {\n        auto create_index_task = std::get<CreateVectorIndexTask>(task_info);\n\n        s = create_index_task.input_segment_->reload_vector_index(\n            *schema_, create_index_task.output_segment_meta_,\n            create_index_task.output_vector_indexers_,\n            create_index_task.output_quant_vector_indexers_);\n        CHECK_RETURN_STATUS(s);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  return The loss is durable the moment that manifest is written; the reopened process never replays the orphaned WAL because replay is gated on the (now removed) writing-block meta.\n\nEverything below is established by reading the frozen tree; I did not build or run anything.\n\n---\n\n## 1. State that differs between recovery and ordinary insertion\n\n**Ordinary insertion path.** `SegmentImpl::Insert/Upsert/Update/Delete` call `append_wal()` *before* mutating memory (`segment.cc:903–918`, 920–948, 950–989). `append_wal()` lazily opens the **member** `wal_file_` (`segment.cc:4324–4340` → `open_wal_file()`, `segment.cc:4303–4322`), then `internal_insert()` lazily creates `memory_store_` (a `MemForwardStore`) and writes id map, forward store, scalar/FTS/vector indexers, `doc_ids_`, and the writing-block counters (`segment.cc:837–881`, `init_memory_components` at 4119–4191). The recovered data is dirty in memory *and* still durable in the untouched on-disk WAL, but nothing in the segment object records \"I have unflushed data\" in a way `flush()` consults.\n\n**Why it can be read initially.** All read paths operate on the live in-memory structures: `Stats()` sums `segment->doc_count()` = `doc_ids_.size()` (`collection.cc:403–442`; `segment.cc:589–600`); `get_all_segments()` includes the writing segment whenever `doc_count() > 0` (`collection.cc:2076–2082`); `Fetch`/`Query` read `memory_store_` and the memory indexers. Moreover, durability at this point is still provided by the WAL + unchanged manifest: a plain reopen (no optimize) would hit `recover()` again. In `SegmentImpl::Open`, `writing_forward_block()` is now `std::nullopt`, so the WAL-replay branch (484–501) is skipped — the WAL file, still sitting at `<coll>/<seg_id>/<block_id>.wal` with every record intact, is never read again (and never deleted; nothing calls `remove()` on a null handle, and the segment directory survives because `CreateVectorIndexTask` inputs are not destroyed, unlike `CompactTask` inputs at `collection.cc:898–901`). `load_persist_scalar_blocks` finds no SCALAR blocks, so `doc_ids_` stays empty (`segment.cc:3913–3957`) → `doc_count()==0`, `Fetch` misses via id-map/segment lookup, documents gone.\n\n**Control (no crash):** in the inserting process `wal_file_` is open with records, so step 3's guard passes and `flush()` performs the full sequence — memory block written to a file, `finish_memory_components()` adds SCALAR/VECTOR_INDEX blocks to the meta, manifest updated, WAL removed — *before* step 4 removes the writing block. The committed manifest references real data files, which reopen loads. No loss.\n\nNote the trigger sharpness: had process B inserted even one document, `append_wal` → `open_wal_file()` would have reopened the existing WAL (`segment.cc:4308–4312`), making `has_record()` true and the subsequent `dump()/flush()` real — masking the bug. That matches the scenario's \"without inserting any additional documents.\"\n\n## 3. Why success + same-handle statistics don't establish durability\n\n- **`Status::OK()` is compositional, not semantic.** Optimize returns OK because each step returned OK; the pivotal step (`dump()`→`flush()`) returned OK through an early-exit that means \"I saw no open WAL handle,\" which the code conflates with \"everything is persisted.\" No step verifies that the segment's documents exist in files referenced by the committed manifest.\n- **Same-handle reads never touch the persisted image.** `Stats()`, `Fetch()`, and `Query()` read `doc_ids_`, `memory_store_`, and memory indexers (`collection.cc:403–442`, 1757–1790; `segment.cc:589–600`), all of which are unchanged in-process — `reload_vector_index` even swaps `segment_meta_` while preserving them (`segment.cc:1882–1940`). The handle cannot observe that the manifest it just committed (`version_manager.cc:282–301`) describes zero forward blocks for those docs. Durability is defined solely by what a *fresh* open loads (`version_manager.cc:190–241`; `segment.cc:461–517`, 3913–3957) — only a reopen (or inspecting manifest/segment files) tests it.\n- An explicit `Collection::Flush()` in process B is equally uninformative: it routes to the same guarded `flush()` (`collection.cc:389–395`) and no-ops.\n\n## 4. Smallest repair principle and regression test (described, not implemented)\n\n**Repair principle:** *a writing segment that replayed WAL records is dirty, and the guard in `flush()` must reflect dirty state rather than handle state.* Minimally, at the end of a successful `recover()` (`segment.cc:4193–4301`), adopt the WAL — e.g., call `open_wal_file()` (4303–4322), which reopens the existing file in append mode — so `wal_file_ != nullptr && has_record()` and the existing `flush()` machinery does what it already does correctly on the ordinary path: write the memory block, run `finish_memory_components()`, commit the meta via `update_version()`, then remove the WAL. This restores the invariant that `switch_to_new_segment_for_writing`'s `remove_writing_forward_block()` (`collection.cc:1538`) and `create_all_vector_index`'s equivalent (`segment.cc:1625`) rely on: the writing-block pointer is dropped only *after* the block's contents are described by persisted blocks in the committed manifest. Optimize proceeds: `persist_segments` = {old segment} (802–803); `build_compact_task` with one segment and no deletes (`rebuild=false`) produces a single `CreateVectorIndexTask` (`collection.cc:991–1002`), executed via `SegmentHelper::ExecuteCreateVectorIndexTask` → `create_all_vector_index` (`src/db/index/segment/segment_helper.cc:1113–1125`; `segment.cc:1617–1640`). With the default index (`DefaultVectorIndexParams` = `FlatIndexParams`, `src/include/zvec/db/index_params.h:437`), the field was already marked indexed at segment creation (`segment.cc:534–539`), so `create_vector_index` hits the skip branch (`segment.cc:1685–1690`) and returns OK having written nothing; its output meta again strips any writing block (1624–1625). (With HNSW params it would merge from `vector_indexers_[column]` — the *persisted* indexer list — which never received the memory indexers because `finish_memory_components()` never ran, `segment.cc:1652–1662`, 4371–4384.)\n6. Optimize commits that meta (`collection.cc:863–868`), `apply` + `flush` again (871–877), and `reload_vector_index` (902–910 → `segment.cc:1882–1940`) swaps the live segment's `segment_meta_` while leaving `memory_store_`/`doc_ids_` intact. `Optimize` returns `Status::OK()` (914).\n\n**Reopen (process C):** `recovery()` loads the new manifest; the old segment is opened as a *persisted* segment (`collection.cc:1861–1874`). In `SegmentImpl::Open`, `writing_forward_block()` is now `std::nullopt`, so the WAL-replay branch (484–501) is skipped — the WAL file, still sitting at `<coll>/<seg_id>/<block_id>.wal` with every record intact, is never read again (and never deleted; nothing calls `remove()` on a null handle, and the segment directory survives because `CreateVectorIndexTask` inputs are not destroyed, unlike `CompactTask` inputs at `collection.cc:898–901`). `load_persist_scalar_blocks` finds no SCALAR blocks, so `doc_ids_` stays empty (`segment.cc:3913–3957`) → `doc_count()==0`, `Fetch` misses via id-map/segment lookup, documents gone.\n\n**Control (no crash):** in the inserting process `wal_file_` is open with records, so step 3's guard passes and `flush()` performs the full sequence — memory block written to a file, `finish_memory_components()` adds SCALAR/VECTOR_INDEX blocks to the meta, manifest updated, WAL removed — *before* step 4 removes the writing block. The committed manifest references real data files, which reopen loads. No loss.\n\nNote the trigger sharpness: had process B inserted even one document, `append_wal` → `open_wal_file()` would have reopened the existing WAL (`segment.cc:4308–4312`), making `has_record()` true and the subsequent `dump()/flush()` real — masking the bug. That matches the scenario's \"without inserting any additional documents.\"\n\n## 3. Why success + same-handle statistics don't establish durability\n\n- **`Status::OK()` is compositional, not semantic.** Optimize returns OK because each step returned OK; the pivotal step (`dump()`→`flush()`) returned OK through an early-exit that means \"I saw no open WAL handle,\" which the code conflates with \"everything is persisted.\" No step verifies that the segment's documents exist in files referenced by the committed manifest.\n- **Same-handle reads never touch the persisted image.** `Stats()`, `Fetch()`, and `Query()` read `doc_ids_`, `memory_store_`, and memory indexers (`collection.cc:403–442`, 1757–1790; `segment.cc:589–600`), all of which are unchanged in-process — `reload_vector_index` even swaps `segment_meta_` while preserving them (`segment.cc:1882–1940`). The handle cannot observe that the manifest it just committed (`version_manager.cc:282–301`) describes zero forward blocks for those docs. Durability is defined solely by what a *fresh* open loads (`version_manager.cc:190–241`; `segment.cc:461–517`, 3913–3957) — only a reopen (or inspecting manifest/segment files) tests it.\n- An explicit `Collection::Flush()` in process B is equally uninformative: it routes to the same guarded `flush()` (`collection.cc:389–395`) and no-ops.\n\n## 4. Smallest repair principle and regression test (described, not implemented)\n\n**Repair principle:** *a writing segment that replayed WAL records is dirty, and the guard in `flush()` must reflect dirty state rather than handle state.* Minimally, at the end of a successful `recover()` (`segment.cc:4193–4301`), adopt the WAL — e.g., call `open_wal_file()` (4303–4322), which reopens the existing file in append mode — so `wal_file_ != nullptr && has_record()` and the existing `flush()` machinery does what it already does correctly on the ordinary path: write the memory block, run `finish_memory_components()`, commit the meta via `update_version()`, then remove the WAL. This restores the invariant that `switch_to_new_segment_for_writing`'s `remove_writing_forward_block()` (`collection.cc:1538`) and `create_all_vector_index`'s equivalent (`segment.cc:1625`) rely on: the writing-block pointer is dropped only *after* the block's contents are described by persisted blocks in the committed manifest. An equivalent alternative is to rebase the guard itself (`segment.cc:2220`) on `memory_store_ != nullptr` / writing-block `doc_count_ > 0`, but that variant must then also handle removing the orphaned on-disk WAL, so adopting the handle in `recover()` is the smaller, more faithful change. Insert nothing in between.
